title: Prompt Library: frontend backend-sync for rich-text colors, improved Word paste, and favicon assets

requirements.summary: Load prompts/categories from backend after login and persist all prompt/category changes (including rich-text colors) to backend, replacing localStorage as source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: After login, the app fetches prompts/categories from the backend and populates the existing Zustand stores used by the UI.
Creating a prompt, editing a prompt (including color changes), deleting, duplicating, and toggling favorite update the backend and then reflect in the UI.
Search results and prompt previews render the stored prompt content via the existing PromptContent component (sanitized HTML) and preserve text colors (do not revert to black).
localStorage auto-persist is no longer the source of truth for prompts/categories once backend persistence is enabled (no overwriting backend-sourced rich text with stale local data).

file_operations.description: Create a small API layer that uses the backend actor (from the core-infrastructure actor configuration) to fetch prompts/categories and perform prompt/category mutations (save/delete/search). Include mapping helpers between backend Prompt/Category types and the app’s Zustand Prompt/category representations, ensuring prompt.content remains an HTML string and is not re-sanitized in a way that strips allowed inline color styling. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Add a React hook that, once the user is authenticated and the actor is available, loads prompts/categories from the backend into the existing Zustand stores and exposes async action wrappers for create/edit/delete/duplicate/favorite/category changes that write to backend first (or write then refresh) and update Zustand on success. Ensure logout clears in-memory prompt/category state. Use authorization guidance to keep app data hidden until logged in and handle unauthorized backend failures gracefully. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Stop loading/saving prompts and categories from/to localStorage as the primary data source once backend persistence is enabled. Keep persisting only non-sensitive UI preferences (e.g., viewMode) to localStorage, and avoid overwriting backend-loaded Zustand state on mount.

Adjust storage schema and helpers to persist only UI preferences needed across refresh (e.g., viewMode), removing prompts/categories from persisted storage to prevent stale rich-text HTML overwriting backend-sourced data.

Add minimal store support needed for backend-sync flow (e.g., a clear/reset action for logout, and/or a replace/upsert helper) without moving CRUD into the store if handled by the sync hook. Ensure store setters can accept backend-loaded prompt arrays without re-sanitizing content.
Add minimal store support needed for backend-sync flow (e.g., clear/reset action for logout, and/or replace/set helpers) so backend-loaded categories become the single source of truth in UI state.

Wire backend-sync into the authenticated app flow: after login, trigger loading prompts/categories from backend and populate Zustand stores; replace direct Zustand mutations (add/update/delete/duplicate/toggle favorite and category changes) with async wrappers that persist to backend and then update UI. Ensure in-memory prompt/category data is cleared on logout (in addition to query cache clearing) per authorization guidance. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Route category rename/delete actions through the backend-sync action wrappers so category edits and deletions are persisted to backend and reflected in prompt/category Zustand state after completion. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

After a successful import into Zustand, persist imported prompts/categories to backend using the backend-sync layer (batch via sequential saves/refresh), so imported rich-text HTML (including colors) round-trips through backend and remains visible in search/previews. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Preserve supported formatting (especially text colors) when pasting from Microsoft Word by capturing clipboard HTML and sanitizing into the app’s allowed HTML subset.
acceptanceCriteria: Pasting from Microsoft Word into the rich text editor keeps text color formatting when the clipboard provides HTML (do not force plaintext-only paste).
The pasted content is sanitized to the app’s safe subset while preserving text color styling where present (e.g., span color styles).
Saving the prompt after a Word paste and then searching/opening the prompt shows the same colors as pasted (within supported formatting).

file_operations.description: Update paste handling to prefer clipboard 'text/html' when available: sanitize the HTML into the allowed subset (preserving span color styles) and insert sanitized HTML into the editor; fall back to plaintext only when HTML is not available. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

Extend/adjust sanitization rules to better support common Word HTML while remaining safe: preserve inline text color styling (e.g., span style color) and keep reasonable structure/line breaks for pasted content, without allowing unsafe tags/attributes. Ensure sanitizer does not normalize all text to black when a color style exists.

Confirm the editor save flow sanitizes pasted HTML once (at save) and does not accidentally strip color styling; ensure the editor’s value/state handling does not overwrite pasted HTML with plaintext. Verify the component's usage instructions before implementing.

requirements.summary: Use the uploaded icon as the browser-tab favicon by adding generated 16x16 and 32x32 PNG assets and referencing them in the HTML.
acceptanceCriteria: The favicon displayed in the browser tab matches the uploaded image.
frontend/index.html references the generated favicon files under /assets/generated/ for 16x16 and 32x32 PNG sizes.
No favicon changes are required beyond the main app tab/favicon behavior.

file_operations.description: Add the generated favicon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_16x16.png (from the provided generated asset list) so it is served as a static file.
Add the generated favicon asset at frontend/public/assets/generated/favicon.dim_32x32.png (from the provided generated asset list) so it is served as a static file.

Ensure favicon link tags reference /assets/generated/favicon.dim_32x32.png and /assets/generated/favicon.dim_16x16.png and remove/avoid any conflicting favicon declarations so the uploaded image is the favicon.
